# tree_coverage AC extraction ignores numbered Acceptance Criteria lists

Discovered-from: SA-0MUY9PMB7001ENMP (plan session for the implement.py claim bug).

## Problem statement

`skill/shared/tree_coverage.py::extract_acceptance_criteria` collects only markdown
bullet (`- ` / `+ `) AC entries. Work items whose `## Acceptance Criteria` section uses an
ordered list (`1. `, `2. `, …) yield **zero** extracted ACs. The plan skill's AC coverage
review (`run_coverage_review`) then reports `fully_covered: True` / `coverage_pct: 100`
trivially, so parent→child AC coverage is never actually verified for those items.

Observed on SA-0MUY9PMB7001ENMP, whose `## Acceptance Criteria` section uses a numbered
list: `run_coverage_review` returned `parent_acs: 0`.

## Users

- Agents running `/skill:plan` AC coverage review, who rely on the coverage recommendation
  (`proceed` / `auto_close` / `stop`) to gate `plan_complete`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `extract_acceptance_criteria` recognises ordered-list AC entries (`1. `, `2) `, etc.)
  as well as `- `/`+ ` bullets, preserving entry order and stripping list markers.
- Bold-led numbered items are handled: `1. **Title.** text` parses to
  `**Title.** text` (text after the marker kept verbatim) — dominant style in the
  tts consumer project (cross-ref TTS-0MVL6TCHF005Z2CC).
- Mixed bullet + numbered sections extract every AC exactly once.
- Unit tests in `skill/shared/tests/` (or the existing test module for `tree_coverage`)
  cover bullet-only, numbered-only, bold-led numbered and mixed AC sections.
- `run_coverage_review` for an item with numbered ACs returns the real AC count (not 0).
- Full project test suite passes.

## Notes

- Can be worked independently of SA-0MUY9PMB7001ENMP; not blocking.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` — `extract_acceptance_criteria`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No clarifying questions required; the behaviour was reproduced directly against
  SA-0MUY9PMB7001ENMP.

## Cross-references

- TTS-0MVL6TCHF005Z2CC (tts consumer worklog) — tracking/discovery record of this
  same bug; its AC4 calls out bold-led numbered items. Planner decision (producer
  delegated): add explicit bold-led numbered AC/test here. Implementation sketch
  and verification steps recorded on that item (Plan block).
data.title: tree_coverage AC extraction ignores numbered Acceptance Criteria lists

data.description:
## Problem

`skill/ship/scripts/release/regenerate-version.js` runs the consumer repo's `npm run build`, then stages with `git add -u` and commits `Regenerate derived version files for v<version>`. When the consumer repo has a git submodule whose build mutates it (e.g. `npm run build` runs `engine:sync`, which advances `./core` to the engine remote tip — main-street's `build` script does exactly this), `git add -u` also stages the submodule **pointer/gitlink**. The derived-files commit then silently bumps the gitlink while the engine pin (`configs/engine-pin.json`) stays unchanged, and the release pin-contract gate fails on the merged tree (observed in the v0.1.22 release attempt, commit `155eead1`: `core` → `9ee194e0` while the pin stayed `d907af9f`).

## Required change (decided in intake MS-0MVN0G6VB000ZF57)

- **Generic gitlink exclusion (option A)**: after `git add -u`, unstage every staged submodule pointer (mode `160000` in `git diff --cached` / `git ls-files --stage`), so the derived-files commit can never contain a submodule pointer change. Consumer-repo agnostic; works for any submodule (`core`, future ones) with no per-repo configuration.
- **Regression tests in BOTH copies** (option A): authoritative `tests/node/test-regenerate-version.mjs` and skill-local `skill/ship/tests/test_regenerate_version.mjs` gain a submodule fixture (local-path submodule, `GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=file`, mirroring main-street's engine-sync tests): an advanced/dirty submodule checkout must not end up in the derived-files commit, and normal tracked-file regeneration still commits.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `regenerateDerivedFiles` never stages submodule pointers: with a fixture repo containing a submodule whose HEAD differs from the recorded gitlink, the derived-files commit contains only regenerated tracked files — the gitlink is unchanged and no commit is made when the only change is the submodule bump.
- Existing behaviour is preserved: no build script → no-op; successful regeneration commits the derived file(s); failing build is non-fatal.
- Both `tests/node/test-regenerate-version.mjs` and `skill/ship/tests/test_regenerate_version.mjs` pass, and the framework's node test suite is green.
- Docs updated as applicable (`docs/dev/release-process.md`, `skill/ship/SKILL.md` derived-files/merge step) noting submodule pointers are excluded from the derived-files commit.

## Constraints

- No change to main-street's `engine:sync`/`engine:verify` design; the pin/verify split (MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED) stays as is.
- The fix must be generic — no `core`-specific hardcoding (alternative B rejected in intake; allow-list C rejected as needing per-repo config).
- Do not alter the release flow's gate ordering (derived-files step stays post-merge, pre-tag).
- Tracks: MS-0MVN0G6VB000ZF57 (tce-main-street worklog) — this MS item is blocked by this SA item.
data.title: Ship release derived-files step must never stage submodule pointer changes (gitlink exclusion)

# Intake Brief — Release blocked: shell worklog-ref gate diverges from the JS gate (fetched-check / tmp-reauthor)

## Problem statement

The canonical release merge script `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` aborts every release with:

```
  - refs/worklog/fetched-check
  - refs/worklog/tmp-reauthor
Error: Dangerous worklog refs detected under refs/worklog/. Aborting release to prevent accidental merge of worklog data into main.
```

Its worklog-ref gate is **out of date** relative to the JavaScript gate that the `run-release.js` wrapper applies minutes earlier (Step 3.5), which passes cleanly.

`wl sync` maintains several bookkeeping refs under `refs/worklog/`, and all of them (including `fetched-check` and `tmp-reauthor`) hold the worklog **data** file `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl`. They are never code branches and are never merged by `git merge`/`git pull`. The JS gate (`check-worklog-refs.js`) was fixed to exclude *any* `refs/worklog/*` ref containing that data file (SA-0MVMD7NTC0086HWK); the shell script was never updated to match, so it only hardcodes an exclusion for the literal ref name `refs/worklog/data`.

Result: the release cannot proceed. Verified live on 2026-10-25 — all wrapper gates 1–3.7 passed, then the merge script exited 1 instantly (the wrapper only prints child stdout, so the stderr reason was hidden).

## Users

- **Release agents / operators** — cannot complete any `dev`→`main` release while the bookkeeping refs exist.
- **The ship skill** — its two gate implementations contradict each other, so the wrapper's green gate is meaningless.

## Goal (user story)

**As a** release operator, **I want** the shell merge script's worklog-ref gate to apply exactly the same rule as `check-worklog-refs.js`, **so that** legitimate `wl sync` bookkeeping refs never block a release while genuine orphan worklog refs still do.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **AC1** — `merge-dev-to-main.sh` does not flag a `refs/worklog/*` ref whose commit contains `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` (covers `refs/worklog/data`, `refs/worklog/fetched-check`, `refs/worklog/tmp-reauthor` and any future bookkeeping ref).
2. **AC2** — A genuine orphan `refs/worklog/*` ref that does **not** contain `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` is still flagged and aborts the release (exit 1) with the ref name printed.
3. **AC3** — `refs/worklog/remotes/**` mirror refs remain excluded (existing behaviour preserved).
4. **AC4** — Automated regression tests cover AC1, AC2 and AC3 by exercising the real gate logic (extracted into a testable helper or run the script against a scratch repository), not by grepping the script source.
5. **AC5** — `skill/ship/SKILL.md` (or the ship reference docs) documents that the shell gate mirrors the JS gate's data-file rule.

## Existing state

- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` lines ~110–142: gate enumerates `git for-each-ref refs/worklog/`, skips `refs/worklog/remotes/*`, and skips `refs/worklog/data` only when `git cat-file -e refs/worklog/data:.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` succeeds. Every other ref sets `DANGEROUS_REFS=1`.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-worklog-refs.js` (the correct, current rule): skips `refs/worklog/remotes/*`; then for each other ref, `git cat-file -e <ref>:.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` → excluded as legitimate bookkeeping, else flagged.
- Live evidence (2026-10-25): `refs/worklog/fetched-check` → contains data file; `refs/worklog/tmp-reauthor` → contains data file; `refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data` → contains data file. The wrapper gate passed; the shell gate aborted.
- Existing unit coverage for the JS gate: `tests/unit/test-check-worklog-refs.mjs`. No test covers the shell gate.

## Desired change

1. **`skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh`** — replace the name-based `refs/worklog/data` special case with the JS gate's content test: for each ref not under `refs/worklog/remotes/`, exclude it when `git cat-file -e "${ref}:.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl"` succeeds; otherwise flag it. Keep the abort message and exit code 1.
2. **Tests** — add regression coverage that runs the real logic (preferred: extract the gate's decision into a small helper the test can invoke, or run the script's gate against a scratch git repo with crafted refs) asserting AC1/AC2/AC3.
3. **Docs** — update the gate comment block and ship reference docs to state the shell gate mirrors `check-worklog-refs.js` (data-file rule, not ref names).

## Constraints

- No behaviour change for genuine orphan refs: they must still block the release.
- Fail-closed on an unreadable ref, matching the JS gate (a ref whose data presence cannot be determined is dangerous).
- Do not weaken the Code Freeze, test-suite or dangerous-ref gating in any other way.
- Do not edit `.pi/` or installed copies; the repo's `skill/` tree is the source of truth (the installed skill is a symlink).

## Key Files

- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh`
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-worklog-refs.js` (reference implementation; read-only unless a shared helper is extracted)
- `tests/unit/test-check-worklog-refs.mjs` (style reference for the new test)
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md`
- `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** loosening the gate could let a genuinely dangerous orphan ref through → mitigated by AC2 and fail-closed semantics.
- **Risk:** shell quoting hazards with ref names → the loop must quote `"${ref}"` consistently.
- **Assumption:** refs holding `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` are always worklog sync bookkeeping, never code — this is the rule the JS gate already relies on.

## Blocking relationship

Blocks the current `dev`→`main` release (all other release gates passed on 2026-10-25). Discovered while running `/skill:ship release`.
data.title: Release blocked: shell worklog-ref gate diverges from JS gate (fetched-check/tmp-reauthor)
